blueprint_sources: Clayton Homes ModSystem 2BR/1BA 28x40 — 14ft wide highway-legal modules, seam connectors at 28ft midpoint
Dvele 3BR/2BA 1,500 sqft two-module stacked layout — module seam at exterior wall with SharkBite connections
Mighty Buildings 3BR/2BA — 3D-printed modules, seam at exterior wall, stub-out connectors at seam face

petronus_classification.note: Prefab modular construction is fundamentally different from site-built — every MEP system must be designed to respect module boundaries. The MODULE SEAM RULE is the governing constraint: no continuous pipe, duct, or wire may cross a module seam except at explicitly designed stub-out connection points. Violating this rule makes on-site assembly impossible.

lot.site_prep_note: Foundation must be engineered specifically for module loads and dimensions. Site must be leveled and compacted before module delivery. Access road must accommodate semi-truck + crane (14ft wide minimum clearance, 100ft turning radius).
lot.note: Site-agnostic from a code perspective (factory-built under state or HUD certification), but site prep and access are critical for modular delivery and craning.

module_geometry.max_width_note: 14ft is the highway transport limit without special wide-load permits. Module width is the hardest constraint in prefab design — never exceed 14ft per module.
module_geometry.module_seam_rule: CRITICAL MODULE SEAM RULE: ALL MEP systems must be designed to stay entirely within a single 3D module. No pipe, duct, or wire may run continuously across a module seam. The ONLY exception is a designated connection stub-out at the exact seam face. This stub-out must use approved coupling types (Fernco flex coupling for DWV, SharkBite or ProPress for supply, listed junction box for electrical).

structure.pier_design_note: Foundation designed to exact module grid dimensions. Pier locations must align with module rim joist bearing points — coordinate with module manufacturer before foundation design.
structure.factory_quality_note: Factory construction offers tighter tolerances than site-built — typically ±1/8in vs ±1/4in. Structural shear is designed into the module box — the module itself acts as a stressed-skin panel. Verify shear design for California SDC D.

floor_program.note: Program is organized by module. Each module contains a complete functional zone. Wet fixtures are clustered per module to keep DWV within the module boundary.

module_1.mep_note: All DWV for this module must drain to stub-out at module seam or sill. Kitchen and half bath wet wall centralized within this module — no DWV runs to adjacent module. PEX supply terminates at module junction box at seam face.

module_2.mep_note: All DWV for this module is self-contained. Connects to Module 1 DWV via Fernco flex coupling at seam face. All circuits home-run to junction box at seam — only seam connector cables cross module boundary.

module_3_optional_second_story.mep_note: Stacked module above Modules 1 or 2. Vertical seam (floor/ceiling) is the seam boundary. All MEP from below passes through designated chase penetrations at exact seam locations — no unsupported runs span the floor/ceiling seam.

wet_wall.note: Each module contains its own wet wall. DWV from each module exits at the seam face via stub-out with Fernco flex coupling. Supply terminates at SharkBite/ProPress fitting at seam. No soldered joints within 6in of seam face — differential thermal movement would crack solder joints during transport.

staircase.stair_module_note: Stair opening is pre-cut in factory. Stair must fit entirely within one module — cannot span a seam. Place at the seam end of a module so upper and lower landings are within the same module footprint.
staircase.mep_note: All vertical MEP at stair location passes through pre-drilled factory sleeves. No field-drilled penetrations through stair stringers or module box structure.

mep_chase.note: MEP chases are contained within each module. At each seam, a factory-installed junction box (electrical), SharkBite fitting (supply), and Fernco coupling (DWV) allow on-site connection. The generator must identify every seam crossing and design an explicit connection point — no implicit continuous runs.

hvac.duct_seam_rule: HVAC ducted systems must be fully contained within each module. Duct stub-outs at seam faces only — on-site connection via flexible duct connector at seam face.

seam_connection.note: Fernco flex couplings at all seam connections accommodate transport vibration and on-site differential settlement. Never use rigid glued or soldered couplings within 6in of seam face.
SharkBite or ProPress fittings at seam face — no soldered joints within 6in of seam. Push-fit allows for the slight misalignment that can occur between modules during site placement.

panel.junction_box_note: Each module has a factory-installed junction box at each seam face. All circuits home-run to the junction box — no continuous wire runs cross the seam. At the junction box, site-installed listed connectors bridge between modules. Listed means UL 514B or equivalent junction box with listed conduit connectors.

seam_connection.note: All module-to-module electrical connections must be made in a listed junction box at the seam face. No single continuous wire may cross the seam — break at junction box with listed connectors.

solar.wiring_seam_note: Solar micro-inverters per panel allow array wiring to be self-contained per module — no DC home runs crossing seams. Use micro-inverter on each panel, AC home run to module junction box.

massing_hints.note: Prefab modern box massing is defined by the 14ft module width constraint. Length is a multiple of module sections. Flat or very low slope roof. Horizontal siding. Large glazing on end walls (not sides, which are often seams). On-site assembly visible as distinct module volumes.

known_constraints_summary: MODULE SEAM RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE): Every MEP run must stay entirely within a single module. Cross-seam connections ONLY at designated stub-out points at the seam face. No diagonal or continuous runs across seams.
DWV cross-seam: Fernco flex coupling only at seam face. No glued joint within 3in, no soldered joint within 6in of seam.
Supply cross-seam: SharkBite or ProPress only at seam face. No soldered joints within 6in of seam.
Electrical cross-seam: listed junction box at seam face. No single continuous wire crosses seam — break at junction box with listed connectors.
HVAC cross-seam: flexible duct connector at duct stub-out at seam face. No rigid duct span across seam.
Module max width is 14ft — this is a highway transport limit. Never exceed 14ft module width.
Foundation must be engineered to exact module grid dimensions — coordinate with module manufacturer before foundation design.
Site access requires semi-truck + crane: 14ft minimum clearance, 100ft turning radius. Verify site access before selecting this archetype.
Solar: use micro-inverters per panel so array wiring stays within each roof module — no DC home runs crossing seams.
Factory construction reduces on-site labor 40-60% but requires exact site prep and crane coordination on installation day.
